stages.title: Idea & opportunity
stages.work: Describe the user, the situation, the existing workaround and the consequence of leaving the problem unsolved.
stages.question: Is the problem specific enough to investigate?
topics: User segments, alternatives and current workarounds
tools: Assumption map — rank uncertainty and impact
stages.lab: Choose a specific customer problem. Write three hypotheses and define what evidence would disprove each one.
criteria: Problem describes a user and a situation
Hypothesis can be tested without building a product

stages.title: Customer validation
stages.work: Prepare neutral interview questions, speak with potential users and separate evidence from enthusiasm. Record disconfirming feedback too.
stages.question: What changed after speaking with users?
topics: Neutral interview questions and avoiding leading prompts
tools: Shared document — interview guide and anonymised notes
Spreadsheet — evidence matrix and recurring patterns
stages.lab: Create a focused interview guide. Prepare for discovery conversations, then synthesise the evidence without turning opinions into demand claims.
criteria: Record contrary evidence and gaps in the sample

stages.title: Business model
stages.summary: Explain who benefits and who may pay.
stages.work: Map the value proposition, alternatives, distribution channels, pricing hypothesis and early cost assumptions.
stages.question: Which commercial assumption is least tested?
topics: Cost drivers and first-pass unit economics
tools: Business Model Canvas — connect users, value and operations
Spreadsheet — price, cost and sensitivity scenarios
stages.lab: Compare two ways to deliver an agreed service. Change demand and support assumptions to see where each model stops making sense.
criteria: Show assumptions and sensitivity, not unsupported revenue projections

stages.title: MVP design & build
stages.work: Choose the smallest prototype that answers a question. Define scope, a success signal and a short user-testing plan before adding features.
stages.question: What learning would justify the next build?
topics: User flows, acceptance criteria and technical feasibility
tools: Paper or Figma — test a workflow before coding
stages.lab: Prototype the route from finding a slot to receiving confirmation. Give a participant a task and observe where they get stuck.
criteria: Define a measurable success signal before running the test

stages.title: Pilot & go-to-market
stages.summary: Find a small, relevant first audience.
stages.work: Prepare a controlled pilot, onboarding instructions and feedback collection. Define what a successful first use looks like.
stages.question: Can a first user reach value without the founder explaining every step?
topics: Data boundaries, permissions and rollback planning
tools: Pilot checklist — responsibilities and stop conditions
Shared feedback log — issues and observed outcomes
stages.lab: Prepare a small pilot plan with entry criteria, a contact person and a manual fallback when a booking cannot be completed.
criteria: User expectations and support ownership are explicit
Pilot has a stop or rollback condition

stages.title: Traction & learning
stages.work: Review adoption, repeat use, user feedback and costs. Use a decision log to choose whether to iterate, narrow the problem or stop.
stages.question: Are the signals stronger than vanity metrics?
topics: Activation, repeat use and meaningful metrics
tools: Spreadsheet — simple funnel and cohort observations
Decision log — evidence behind the next experiment
stages.lab: Review a pilot: 20 invitations, 8 first uses and 3 repeat users. Identify what you can conclude and what requires a follow-up conversation.
criteria: Keep sample size and time window visible
Do not confuse interest, usage and willingness to pay

stages.title: Readiness & next steps
stages.work: Document the product, delivery risks, operating needs and learning to date. Shape a clear narrative for collaborators or potential supporters.
stages.output: Delivery case study and next-step brief
stages.question: What is demonstrated, what is assumed and what still needs work?
topics: Demo narratives and evidence-backed next steps
tools: Demo / brief — explain the problem, evidence and next ask
stages.lab: Prepare a five-minute demonstration and a one-page next-step brief. Separate what works now from what needs resources or more validation.
criteria: Next ask is specific, bounded and justified
